steps: Shape your dominant hand into a C, with the thumb and fingers curved toward each other.
Close your non-dominant hand into a fist, with the thumb resting along the front of the fingers.
Rest the thumb of your C hand on the back of the fist, just behind the knuckles.
Tap the thumb up and down against the back of the fist, once or twice, in a straight vertical motion.
Keep the movement up and down only — never circle the thumb around.
Hold the fist steady in front of your chest and keep your face calm and neutral while signing.
tip: Think of the ROCK sign with a C hand — the thumb taps the rock to build the church.

steps: Curl both hands into O shapes, with each thumb touching the fingertips.
Hold the O hands out in front of you, below chest height, with the palms facing each other and angled slightly forward.
Push both hands forward in one quick motion, letting them drift slightly outward as they go.
Shake your head once to the side as the hands move forward.
Sign it lower and quicker than TEACH — the whole motion is small and direct.
tip: Unlike TEACH, the hands angle outward and sit low — one headshake seals the meaning.

steps: Make an A handshape with your dominant hand — a fist with the thumb resting up along the side.
Extend the index finger of your non-dominant hand and hold it out in front of you.
Brush the side of your dominant fist upward against the top edge of that index finger.
Repeat the brushing motion once or twice, keeping it small and controlled.
Keep the non-dominant index finger planted and steady while the fist brushes past it.
tip: Picture polishing a shoe — you are polishing up your skills.
